verbatim_critique:
[D0.5.G cold referee] delivered tier=incremental below novelty_target=field (floor=field). The quotient identification is proved only under the load-bearing all-order restriction that every latent cumulant-shift vector lies in the plane generated by the observed low-order treatment contrasts; the note gives constructions satisfying this condition but does not derive it from a natural primitive model. The advertised if-and-only-if frontier is confined to a union whose no-breakout branch is defined by requiring the legal unequal-effect swap that supplies nonidentification, so it is not a characterization of the broader simultaneous-shift model. The TL;DR's claim of sharp weak-flag rates on bounded shells overstates the theorem: uniform upper bounds hold for arbitrary fixed admissible classes, while matching lower bounds and the consistency converse are proved only for one specially constructed compatible experiment. These restrictions leave the contribution specialized and limit its practical relevance, particularly because the proposed Sachs application supplies no evidence that the latent-plane condition holds. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]

HALTED AT TRIAGE: the math panel returned `revise` and its findings were never repaired, so this note is NOT established as mathematically sound — do not bank it as downgraded on this verdict alone. Open findings: frontier_positioning@thm:population-identification-frontier, related_work_incomplete@thm:population-identification-frontier
